Team / Sara —

Thanks for sending the Lumos redlines. Attached is a suggested counter-proposal: redwood_proposed_indemnity_redline.docx. Summary of our position and recommended compromise:

1) Defense control: Redwood to retain right to control the defense for third-party IP claims where the claim arises from our model or service delivery. We will not unreasonably withhold assignment of counsel to Lumos for claims that are limited to customer-controlled integrations, provided Lumos gives prompt notice and cooperates.

2) Reimbursement & cap: Redwood will indemnify for amounts finally awarded against Redwood up to the order form amount (cap = fees paid in previous 12 months) for third-party IP claims where Redwood is judged liable. This preserves a commercial, predictable exposure.

3) AI-output carve: Exclude from indemnity any claims that are solely based on customer-generated prompts or outputs from open-input prompts absent Redwood's breach of the MSA or misconduct. We will accept liability where Redwood has materially altered model behavior outside normal parameters.

4) Notice & cure: Lumos must provide written notice within 30 days of becoming aware; Redwood requests 45 days for initial response/cure where technically feasible. Tolling while both parties investigate.

5) Evidence/subrogation: Standard cooperation, with Redwood able to pursue subrogation against the original infringer.

Fallbacks: If Lumos insists on full customer control with no oversight, propose an insurance/escrow alternative (insurance certificate or escrow holdback equal to 100% of the order form cap until claim resolution).

Please review the attached markup. Key legal risks called out in the comments — particularly around indemnity for AI-generated output and notification timing. Happy to hop on a 20–30m call if helpful.

—Kim

Thanks for the thorough read and the proposed language. Lumos reviewed Redwood's counter and we're comfortable moving forward on the following basis:
